sources.quote: Tuomo Suntola was born in 1943 in Tampere, Finland.
In 1963, Suntola started his studies on electrical engineering at Helsinki University of Technology (HUT-Teknillinen korkeakoulu, TKK, nowadays Aalto University).

In the autumn of 1971, the Semiconductor Laboratory received its ﬁrst industrial order, a task to develop a miniature solid-state humidity sensor for Vaisala Oy, a Finnish company specializing in meteorological instrumentation.
In the beginning of 1974, Suntola and the small humidity sensor team moved from VTT to Instrumentarium (Ahertajantie 3, Tapiola, Espoo, Finland).
The actual invention of ALE matured in early June 1974.
In 1987, Tuomo Suntola was offered the chance to set up Microchemistry Ltd, as a subsidiary of Neste, for the development of ALE-based solar panels.
In 1987, Tuomo Suntola was offered the chance to set up Microchemistry Ltd, as a subsidiary of Neste, for the development of ALE-based solar panels.
In the same year, Suntola joined Picosun Oy, first as the scientific adviser and, since 2007, as a board member.

The year 2004 brought a delightful surprise to Suntola in the form of the European SEMI Award 2004 "Honoring the Pioneer in Atomic Layer Deposition Techniques … that paved the way for the development of nanoscale semiconductor devices ".

As of 2014, Suntola continues as a board member of Picosun Oy, the chairman of the Physics Foundations Society, and a board member and a frequent lecturer in the Finnish Society for Natural Philosophy.

Since the mid-1990s, with early roots extending to the late 1960s, Suntola has worked on a holistic picture of reality published in 2011 in the book "The Dynamic Universe – toward a uni ﬁed picture of physical reality ".
